## Purpose

List pages in this dashboard do not render a flat table; they bucket rows into labelled sections — Activity groups sessions by work kind, Sessions groups them by category, Knowledge splits real knowledge from measured friction. The `*Section` type is the page-local contract between a pure grouping function and the render loop: a stable key, a display label, and the rows. Keeping the grouping pure and memoised means the ordering rules (priority buckets first, the null bucket last, the attribution-leak rows at the tail) live in one readable place instead of being smeared across JSX.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/pages/** · Extension: .tsx · Files of this role in this subproject: 3

- The bucket type is a page-local, NOT exported `interface <Page>Section { key: string; label: string; <rows>: T[] }` — `ActivitySection` in `Activity.tsx` and `SessionSection` in `Sessions.tsx` are the same three fields over `SessionRow[]`.
- It is produced by one pure function declared right below it (`groupByKind`, `groupSessions`) returning `<Page>Section[] | undefined`. `undefined` is the deliberate "still loading" signal — both return early when `data` is undefined — so the page can distinguish loading from a genuinely empty list.
- Bucketing uses a `new Map<string, T[]>` fill, then an explicit sort over `[...buckets.keys()]`: a module-level `PRIORITY_ORDER` array pins the leading buckets, a `NULL_BUCKET` sentinel is forced last, and everything else falls back to `localeCompare` on the label. Within a bucket the backend's arrival order is preserved, with the special rows pushed to the tail.
- The page memoises the call: `const sections = useMemo(() => groupSessions(data), [data])` — Activity passes the translator into the grouping and lists it in the deps (`[data, t]`) because labels are resolved there.
- What all three pages really share is only this: the outer render is a `flex flex-col` column over the buckets, each child keyed by the bucket key, and each bucket is a *head* carrying its label and its count sitting over a *body* that lists that bucket's rows. Head and body are exactly what varies, and the variation tracks the row component. Two of the three take the **list form** — a `<DataCard>` wrapping a `<ul className="flex flex-col">` of row components — under one of two sanctioned heads: `Sessions.tsx:322-338` is the open one (`gap-6` outer, then a `gap-2` wrapper per section holding `<SectionHeader title={section.label} right={section.sessions.length} />` from `@/components/page`), and `Activity.tsx:604-621` is the collapsible one (`gap-3` outer, each section a `<CollapsibleGroup label={section.label} count={…} defaultOpen={idx === 0}>` that is its own wrapper) — Activity imports no `SectionHeader` at all. The third takes the **card-grid form** and is genuinely bespoke: `Knowledge.tsx:251-270` groups the browse rows by kind with a hand-rolled head (a `<KnowledgeBadge>` plus a raw count `<span>`, `Knowledge.tsx:254-262`) over a `<div className="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2 gap-2">` of `<KnowledgeCard>` — no `DataCard`, no `<ul>`, neither sanctioned head. That is not drift: `KnowledgeCard` already paints its own `border border-border rounded p-3` surface (`features/knowledge/KnowledgeCard/index.tsx:13`), so a `DataCard` around it would double the chrome, and a responsive one-to-two-column grid of cards is not a row list. The same file's `FrictionSection` (`Knowledge.tsx:342-362`) is back on the list form — `SectionHeader` + `DataCard` + `<ul>` — because a friction row *is* a row. Pick `CollapsibleGroup` when the page has many buckets and the reader scans one at a time, `SectionHeader` when every bucket stays open, and the bare grid only when the row component is already a self-contained card.
- The page distinguishes three states explicitly: no project (`EmptyState` inside `PageSurface`), `sections.length === 0` (a different `EmptyState` with its own copy), and loaded.
- Labels come from the i18n helper (`useT()` in `Activity.tsx` and `Knowledge.tsx`); `Sessions.tsx` uses a local `CATEGORY_LABELS` map with a capitalise fallback for unmapped values instead — prefer the i18n route on new pages.
- A section that owns real rendering logic becomes its own page-local component taking its data as a prop (`FrictionSection({ friction })` in `Knowledge.tsx`), still unexported, with a doc comment explaining why the section is kept separate from its neighbours.

## How to apply

Add the interface, the grouping function and the priority constants near the bottom of the page file, above the page's exported component. Return `undefined` while data is undefined, keep the function pure (pass `t` in rather than calling a hook inside), memoise the call in the component, and render through `DataCard` + a `<ul>` under either section head — `SectionHeader` or `CollapsibleGroup` — unless your row component already carries its own card surface, in which case follow `Knowledge.tsx` and lay the cards out directly under a head of your own. Do not export the section type — if two pages need the same grouping, lift the row type to `src/lib` and the rendering to `@/components/page` instead of sharing the page-local bucket.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Activity.tsx — `ActivitySection` + `groupByKind(data, t)` with `PRIORITY_ORDER`, the null bucket last, the leak rows sorted to the tail, and the `CollapsibleGroup` render loop.
- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Sessions.tsx — `SessionSection` + `groupSessions(data)`, then the `SectionHeader`/`DataCard`/`<ul>` render loop.
- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Knowledge.tsx — two shapes in one file: the component form (`FrictionSection`, an unexported section component with its own `SectionHeader`, `DataCard` and empty state) and the card-grid exception (the browse loop at `:251-270`, a hand-rolled head over a two-column grid of `KnowledgeCard`).
